result.note: NITI Aayog school education report of May 2026: tested institution vs enrolment shares and the GER and dropout figures.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about the NITI Aayog report on school education released in May 2026:
items: Government schools make up 68.1% of all schools in India.
Private schools make up 38.8% of all schools in India.
Only 5.4% of schools offer continuous education from Grade 1 to 12.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 2 is wrong: private schools are 23.1% of institutions, and 38.8% is their share of enrolment. Government schools, though 68.1% of all schools, now enrol only 49.24% of students, down from 71% in 2005.
questions.source: Private schools, at 23.1% of institutions, now account for 38.8% of enrolment.

questions.prompt: Consider the following pairs relating to school education data in the NITI Aayog report released in May 2026:
items: Gross Enrolment Ratio at primary level — 90.9%
Gross Enrolment Ratio at higher secondary level — 58.4%
Schools with zero student enrolment that still receive funding — nearly 80,000
questions.ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.explain: The report flagged nearly 8,000 schools, not 80,000, with zero enrolment that still get funding and staff because of outdated records. The fall in GER from 90.9% at primary to 58.4% at higher secondary means nearly four in ten children leave before finishing school.
questions.source: The Gross Enrolment Ratio (GER) drops from 90.9% at primary level to 58.4% at higher secondary.
